newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Turkey threatens to block WEU missions.
newsitem.headline: Turkey threatens to block WEU missions.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller threatened on Tuesday to block the use of NATO equipment by the Western European Union (WEU) because of Greek objections to Ankara's participation in WEU activities.
"Turkey will block all the support of NATO," Ciller was quoted as telling Turkish reporters at a news conference on the margins of a WEU ministerial meeting in the Belgian seaside town of Ostend.
"The WEU can do nothing without the support of NATO," she said.
A correspondent for the Turkish daily newspaper Turkiye said Ciller has been very angry and had left the ministerial meeting immediately after her news conference.
Turkish reporters said Ciller had said that Greece had threatened to block Turkey, an associate member of the WEU, from taking part in WEU missions.
Greece is a full member of the WEU. Both countries are members of NATO.
The WEU, the European Union's fledgling defence arm, plans to conduct peacekeeping and humanitarian aid missions using equipment lent by the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
NATO, with the blessing of the United States, agreed to lend its materiel to the WEU when Europeans wanted to act alone, particularly without the United States.
As a member of NATO, Turkey can veto the use of alliance equipment by the WEU.
Ciller said it was time Greece, a longtime rival, viewed issues in a global manner, Turkish reporters said.
The two countries almost came to war earlier this year over uninhabited islets in the Aegean. The United States stepped in to broker a deal easing the tension.
